content: Hey, I wanted to start a new project to keep track of my personal finances. I've been spending way too much lately.
Actually, before we get into that, I should mention I'm severely allergic to peanuts. Just adding that to my profile so you know.
So back to the finance tracker. I want to build it using Next.js and Tailwind. I really like the glassmorphism aesthetic.
Oh wait, my dog is barking at the mailman again. His name is Max, he's a Golden Retriever and he hates Tuesdays for some reason.
Anyway, for the database, I think I'll go with PostgreSQL. I've used MongoDB before but relational data just makes more sense for finances.
What tech stack was I planning to use for the frontend of my finance app?
I also need a name for the app. Maybe something like 'VaultTracker' or 'PennyWise'. I'll think about it.
By the way, my secret vault code for my physical safe is 8842. Remind me never to write that down anywhere public.
I'm feeling really hungry. I think I might make some pasta for lunch. I've been trying this new garlic and olive oil recipe.
Speaking of recipes, I grew up in a small town in Oregon, and my grandma used to make the best blueberry pies.
Hey, what kind of database did I decide to use for my finance project?
Okay, the pasta was amazing. Back to work. I think I'll add an authentication layer using NextAuth.
Actually, someone on Twitter just mentioned that Clerk is way easier to set up than NextAuth. Maybe I'll pivot to Clerk.
My all-time favorite movie is The Matrix from 1999. I don't know why I just thought of that, probably because I'm looking at green code on my terminal.
I need to go to the grocery store later. I'm completely out of milk and coffee beans.
What is the name of my dog, and what breed is he?
I just checked my bank account and I spent $400 on takeout last month. This finance tracker app is definitely necessary.
I'm going to set my monthly budget goal to $2000 total. If I go over that, the app should send me an angry notification.
Just watched a tutorial on how to use D3.js for charts. I'm going to use it to build a beautiful pie chart of my expenses.
Wait, did I decide to use NextAuth or something else for authentication?
I think I'll name the app 'VaultTracker' after all. It sounds secure.
I'm taking a break to play some guitar. I've been learning Spanish Romance, it's such a beautiful classical piece.
Ugh, I broke my high E string. I need to order new strings on Amazon. I usually get the Ernie Ball regular slinky.
What is my absolute favorite movie?
Okay, strings ordered. Back to the app. I need to design the database schema. I'll have a Users table and a Transactions table.
The Transactions table will have an amount, a date, a category, and a boolean flag for 'is_recurring'.
I just realized I should probably add a way to upload receipts. Maybe I can integrate an OCR library later.
Where did I grow up as a kid?
My friend Sarah just texted me. We're going to a Thai restaurant tonight. I'll have to log that in the new app once it's built.
I need to make sure the Thai place doesn't use peanut oil. That would be a disaster.
Why would it be a disaster if the Thai place uses peanut oil? Do I have a medical issue?
I'm going to deploy the app on Vercel. It's just so much easier for Next.js apps than setting up AWS.
I also bought a domain name: vaulttracker.io. It cost me $40, but I think it's worth it.
I'm thinking of writing a blog post about how I built this. I could post it on Hashnode or Medium.
What did I decide to name my personal finance app?
Actually, I'll go with Hashnode for the blog. It's more developer-focused.
It's getting late. I'm going to head to the restaurant to meet Sarah now.
Dinner was great! We had Pad Thai (no peanuts!) and split a mango sticky rice.
What is my monthly budget limit going to be set to in the app?
I'm exhausted. I'm going to lock up the house. Time to hit the hay.
Just to make sure I don't forget it, what is the secret code to my physical vault?
